packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-09 - UNVERIFIED BLIND IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context proposed an identification or reading for this packet. I did not try to identify the work or author. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..014 in this packet directory, plus a directory listing and an image-size check (sips) of my own packet files. I did nothing beyond the stated rules.

Conventions: (x) = proposed expansion; word? = uncertain; [illegible] = unread; [...] = text lost at edge/fold. Line numbers count from the top of the named image. Modern pencil foliation "Stams, STA, Frag. 120r" / "120v" seen on the margins, not transcribed as text.

======================================================================
LAYOUT SURVEY
======================================================================
image-001 = face A overview (pencil "...120r"); tiles image-002..007.
image-008 = face B overview (pencil "...120v"); tiles image-009..014.

Observations:
- Single leaf, single column, held flat by four acrylic weights. Edges folded in (top and bottom folds; outer margin strip folded on face A right / face B left). The leaf has been used in a binding (slits, folds, holes along a horizontal band at about mid-height).
- Dry-point/hard-point ruling clearly visible; about 22-25 written lines.
- Script: an early, rounded minuscule (Caroline-type), brown ink, a few abbreviations (e(st) as e with stroke, -b; for -bus, q: for -que, macron for m/n).
- Face B: a red marginal chapter number "J xxxiii" (red paragraph-type sign plus numeral) in the left margin beside a large brown/ink initial I that projects into the margin. No other rubrication seen.
- Face B: large looping brownish strokes overlie the left part of many lines (S- and loop-shapes in the margin and across words). These look like a separate, larger cursive script or an offset from an adjoining sheet; I cannot tell which. They are not transcribed.
- Face A: text is almost entirely abraded/faded. Only a column of reddish-brown word-ends at the far left (left of the ruled frame) and a few words inside the frame are visible; the bottom two lines, on the folded-in strip, are clear.
- No glosses or interlinear additions identified.

Tentative interpretation (not identification): prose text on medical/material topics (mentions of medici, humor, malagma, malactica, sebum/adeps of various animals), with a numbered chapter "xxxiii" beginning a section on fats ("De adipibus"). I infer nothing about author, date or provenance.

Selected spans: face B lines 2-7 (upper legible block) and lines 14-24 (lower block, including chapter xxxiii opening). Face A: the bottom two lines and the few legible words in the lower half. Unread: face B line 1 and most of lines 8-13 (very faded, overlaid by loops); almost all of face A.

======================================================================
FACE B (most legible) - single column
======================================================================
Line numbers here are per image; image-009 and image-010 are the upper-left and upper-right halves of the same lines (they overlap in the middle), so I give the joined reading where the halves meet. "|" marks where I joined the two tiles.

     (009 shows "indemudus aut[...]"; 010 shows "[...]us autumis possit? uel si sit frequens c")
L3  (009 L7 / 010 L7)  [...]e? cibu(m) docen | t? medici q(uo)n(iam)? intellegende? mo[...]

======================================================================
FACE A (badly abraded)
======================================================================

             ex? ?lu?rinoso? quodam sed spisso aro[...]
             (007 confirms "[...]da(m) sed spisso aro"; "ex?lurinoso" first word uncertain)
image-007 penultimate (folded strip): [...]rom? iacat? uite? [...]

Everything else on face A: [illegible] at this resolution. Raking light or UV/multispectral imaging would be needed.

======================================================================
LIMITATIONS
======================================================================
- Face A is almost entirely illegible; the few words given are low-confidence except the bottom folded-in lines.
- Face B: large looping strokes overlie the text, which makes the left halves of many lines unreliable. Lines 8-13 (middle block) are largely unread.
- Folded edges (top, bottom, outer margin) hide parts of lines; the bottom-most face A lines are on the folded strip itself.
- I could not resolve the words right after the initial I of chapter xxxiii; the reading "Incip(it)" is tentative.
- Animal-fat words (leopardinum, ursinum, taurinum, sebum, anserin-) are fairly clear; most other content words above are uncertain.
